description: Job Description IMPORTANT : This position is offered within the framework of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme and is open exclusively to nationals of Norway . Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements established for the JPO Programme and the specific requirements of the position. The UNDP Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme The UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) JPO Programme equips outstanding young leaders with the skills and experience required to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and make a positive difference in the world. As a pathway into the world of development, the programme offers young professionals excellent exposure to multilateral cooperation and sustainable development while providing a valuable entry point into the UN system. During their assignments, JPOs benefit from the guidance of experienced UNDP staff members and are actively involved in supporting the design and implementation of UNDP’s programs within UNDP’s headquarters, regional or country offices. Additionally, the JPO will undergo a journey of exposure and growth which will build both personal and professional capacity for a career within the multilateral development sector. As a JPO and young professional in UNDP you should be interested in pursuing a global career with aspiration to work for a field-based organization in support of the development agenda. The JPO will work as part of a team and be supervised by an experienced UNDP staff member, including : Structured guidance and feedback, especially in the beginning of the assignment, with the purpose of gradually increasing of responsibilities Establishment of a work plan, with clear key results Guidance and advice in relation to learning and training opportunities within the field of expertise Completion of the yearly UNDP Annual Performance Review (APR) including learning and development objectives. The JPO will benefit from the following learning and development opportunities: Participation in a virtual Programme Policy and Operations Induction Course within the first 4 to 6 months of assignment Use of yearly JPO duty-related travel and training allocation (DTTA), as per the online DTTA guide On-going Masterclasses on relevant and inspiring themes Career development support mechanisms and activities Networking with fellow JPOs, young professionals and senior UNDP colleagues Mentoring programme Other training and learning opportunities Organisational context The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is supporting the Government of Ethiopia in the implementation of the National Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration Programme (NDRP) as part of broader efforts to consolidate peace and support recovery in conflict-affected regions. The NDRP is being implemented in diverse and politically sensitive settings, including Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, and other areas affected by conflict. These regions vary significantly in terms of their political dynamics, levels of insecurity, and the socio-economic realities faced by ex-combatants and host communities. In this context, the need for clear, consistent, and conflict-sensitive communication is paramount. The dissemination of DDR objectives and progress must be tailored to regional specificities while ensuring alignment with national narratives. title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes présélectionnées seront contactées, généralement dans les deux semaines suivant la date de clôture

title: Physiotherapist
description:
The Physiotherapist is responsible for the treatment, counselling, preventative care and rehabilitation of the motor function and physical wellness of the patients. is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating individualized rehabilitation programs for patients with limb loss and other mobility impairments. Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. description:
What we do
 
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) works worldwide to provide humanitarian protection and assistance to people affected by conflict and armed violence. We take action in response to emergencies and at the same time promote respect for international humanitarian law. We are an independent and neutral organization, and our mandate stems essentially from the Geneva Conventions of 1949. We work closely with National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and with their International Federation in order to ensure a concerted, rational and rapid humanitarian response to the needs of the victims of armed conflict or any other situation of internal violence. We direct and coordinate the international activities conducted in these situations.
 Purpose
 
Language is at the heart of humanitarian action; it enables dialogue, builds trust, and ensures that people affected by conflict can express themselves and be heard.
 
The ICRC Interpreter plays a critical role in enabling this by facilitating accurate and meaningful communication among ICRC delegates, affected populations, authorities, and other stakeholders. Through interpretation in sensitive and complex contexts, including protection activities, visits to detainees, family reunification processes, and dialogue with parties to conflict, the Interpreter ensures that every conversation can take place with clarity, respect, and confidentiality.
 
This is a unique, people-centered role that goes beyond translating words. It requires judgment, cultural awareness, and a deep understanding of the humanitarian principles guiding the ICRC’s work, helping build bridges of understanding where communication can make a real difference.
 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 

Oral interpretation: from Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya to English and vice versa during confidential interviews with people deprived of liberty, ICRC institutional dissemination, ICRC dialogue with authorities, activities to establish the family links which includes delivering Red Cross messages, family tracing and visits to families of detainees.
Written translation: translation of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya languages (newspaper articles, correspondence, etc.) into written English.
Analysis and reporting as required: analysis of conditions of detention, security and other matters relating to the ICRC's mandate.
Can be asked to provide support on other protection activities as needed.

 Relationships
 

Externally, interacts with the authorities, representatives of other organizations and beneficiaries, both within and outside places of detention. May be called upon to develop a network of contacts related to operational needs.
Internally, interacts with staff in other departments.

 Required profile and skills
 

Excellent command of English (C1) required
Excellent command of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya (C1) required
Proficiency in at least two of the above languages is considered a strong asset.
Proficiency in other ICRC operational languages (English, French, Spanish, Russian, Arabic, Portuguese) is a strong asset.
2 years of professional experience. Previous interpreter or translator experience is an advantage.
Strongly motivated by humanitarian work.
Able to work under pressure in a potentially dangerous environment.
Open-minded and adaptable.
University education/degree in interpretation or translation is an advantage.

 Our operational & field constraints
 

In line with the principle of neutrality, the ICRC does not assign personnel to a country of which they are nationals.
Candidates must be in good health and will have to do a medical check-up prior to departure in the field.
Candidates must possess a driving licence (for manual transmission vehicles).
Candidates must be prepared to accept unaccompanied postings (i.e. no spouse, partner, children or dependents) for the first two missions (minimum 12 months each)  or total of 24 months.

 What we offer
 

Rewarding work in a humanitarian and multicultural environment
A two-week orientation course and other opportunities for further in-house training
Attractive social benefits
Join an ICRC talent pool and be considered for future assignments elsewhere

The ICRC values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates!
 Our values
 
At the ICRC, we value impact, collaboration, respect, and compassion. We seek candidates who demonstrate behaviors based on these shared values. For more information on the ICRC values, please visit this page.
